I found two inconsistencies that break the registry contract. Every other carrier quotes in cents for a weight in kg and has the same four methods: `rate`, `label`, `valid_label` and `tracking_url`.

### 1. `shop/carriers/maple.py` takes weight in grams, not kg
The other 19 carriers have `PER_KG` / `MAX_KG` and a docstring saying "weight in kg". Maple has `PER_GRAMS = 3` and `MAX_GRAMS = 30000`, its docstring says "weight in grams", and `rate()` checks and prices `weight` as grams (`maple.py:16-20`).

Callers of the registry pass the same `weight` to any carrier, so Maple gives wrong answers without raising an error:
- `get("maple").rate(5.0)` treats 5 kg as 5 g and returns `int((494 + 3*5) * 1.0)` = **509 cents**. A kg-based rate in the same range as the others would be roughly 2,100 cents, so Maple massively undercharges.
- The range check is off by 1000×. Any weight up to 30,000 "kg" is accepted, so oversized parcels that every other carrier rejects with `ValueError` get quoted.

This one is the more dangerous of the two because no error is raised.

### 2. Four carriers have no `tracking_url()`
`shop/carriers/delta.py`, `kestrel.py`, `onyx.py` and `tundra.py` stop after `valid_label()`. All the others define `tracking_url(code)`. Anything that loops over `REGISTRY` or calls `get(name).tracking_url(...)` will raise `AttributeError` for those four.

### What I checked
- I compared every module against `acme.py` after replacing the carrier names. The only other differences are the expected per-carrier constants (base rate, per-kg rate, zone factors, max weight) and TODO owners.
- All carriers use the same zone keys (`local`/`regional`/`national`) and the same label format (`NAME-%08d` with a matching regex), and every class name matches its `REGISTRY` entry.
- Nothing in `shop/` outside `carriers/` currently calls `REGISTRY`, `get()` or `tracking_url`. Both problems are breaks in the shared interface that will hit the first caller that uses it, not failures you can see in current code.

I didn't edit any files.
